prompt: News organisations sometimes publish stories that later turn out to be false. Some people believe that the law should require corrections to be given the same prominence as the original story. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Nowadays, the news organisations sometimes publish the stories which are not true, and later they must correct them. Some people believe that the law should force them to put the correction in the same place like the original story. I think this idea is good, but there are also some difficulties for the news companies.

Firstly, when a false story is published on the front page, many people read it and they believe it. If the correction is published in a small box in the last page, nobody will see it. So the wrong information stays in the mind of the people. This is very bad for the society, because people take their decisions from the news. For example, if a newspaper writes that a food is dangerous and it is not true, the company can lose all the business, and a small correction can not repair this damage.

Secondly, we should also think about the news organisations. They are publishing hundreds of news every day and mistakes are happening naturally. If the law is very strict, they will be afraid to publish the important stories, and this is also bad for the society because the journalists must be free. Moreover, the correction takes the valuable space which can be used for other news.

In conclusion, I agree that the corrections should be more visible than now, because the false news is very bad for the society, but I think the law should not be too strict with the news organisations, otherwise the freedom of press will be effected.
title: Making corrections as prominent as the story
